symptom: `check -p --references` passed a microflow in an ordinary module that used a Hidden attribute or association of a Usable entity in a Protected (add-on) module; mxbuild then refused it with CE1406 "… is not allowed to use attribute 'AddOn.Request.Payload' because app modules cannot reference hidden elements in add-on modules" (mendixlabs/mxcli#1498).
cause: validateProtectedModuleRefs judged entity, microflow and page targets only; nothing resolved the members a flow uses against their export level, which the semantic model did not carry until ako/mxcli#1518.
fix: checkFlowMembers (validate_protected_module_members.go): over walkTypedFlow — the variable-typing walk extracted from validate_member_refs.go so both checks share it — resolve change/create members, association retrieves, XPath steps of a database retrieve and `$v/…` expression paths (return, declare, set, decision, while, log, call arguments, member values) to attributes (through generalizations) and associations (hops via associationTargetFrom), and report CE1406 when the member's module is Protected, the flow's is not, and the member is Hidden — script-stated level, else stored, else Hidden for a script-created one. The hint is the alter statement with the stored type restated.
insight: Measure every shape before checking it, one microflow per shape so mx check's 'at <activity>' attributes each CE1406: on 11.14.0 all nine uses (change/create attribute and association member, association retrieve, XPath attribute and association, expression attribute and association) were refused and the Usable controls and in-module uses were clean, so the rule is 'any use', not a list of activities. The check is only safe as far as variable typing reaches: anything unresolved — an untyped variable, an association with no stored ends, a Module.Entity.Attribute member — is silent rather than reported, because a false refusal blocks exec. Do not copy the variable-typing walk: two copies drift on which statements type a variable (the duplicate-resolver-drift class), so extract it.
